title: In Vitro Synergism and Preliminary In Vivo Efficacy of Florfenicol Combined with Oxytetracycline against Streptococcus agalactiae Infection in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
content:
ABSTRACT

Streptococcus agalactiae is one of the most serious diseases in Nile tilapia aquaculture. The objective of this study was to evaluate the potential combinational therapy of florfenicol (FF) and oxytetracycline (OTC) against S. agalactiae strains. Checkerboard microdilution assays of FF + OTC showed that among 10 S. agalactiae isolates, 9 were synergistic and 1 was additive. In the efficacy test, Nile tilapia juveniles were divided into 6 groups (in triplicate): control, FF 10 mg/kg/day, FF 20 mg/kg/day, OTC 50 mg/kg/day, OTC 100 mg/kg/day and a combination of FF 10 + OTC 50 mg/kg/day. Each fish was injected intraperitoneally with a resistant isolate of S. agalactiae at 108 CFU and treated with antibiotics via medicated feeds twice daily for 7 days. The survival rate of the FF + OTC combination was 100%, significantly higher than the control (23.33%), low-dose OTC (43.33%) and FF groups (53.33%). The total bacterial counts in the liver of FF + OTC-treated fish were significantly lower than those of the control group (1.05 and 5.15 × 107 CFU/g, respectively). This preliminary study demonstrates that the FF + OTC combination was effective against S. agalactiae infections.
